issues.legal_issue: The statutory power to restore tribal land must be exercised within a reasonable time, even when the statute prescribes no specific limitation period and the transfer is alleged to be fraudulent.
material_facts: The transfer at issue occurred in 1938, and the restoration application was made in 1978.
The restoration authority treated the surrender and subsequent settlement as a single transaction and ordered restoration; the lower authorities and High Court upheld that order.
Fraud was alleged, and the Court assumed for the purpose of its analysis that the transaction was fraudulent.
The Court found that the transfer had not been shown to contravene a provision of the Act in force when it occurred.
issues.conclusion: The restoration authority could not properly exercise its power after the unreasonable delay in this case; the restoration order and the judgments upholding it were set aside.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 71A of the Chota Nagpur Tenancy Act, 1908, the words at any time do not authorize an unguided exercise of power without regard to delay. Although the Limitation Act, 1963, including Article 65, does not prescribe the deadline for this administrative restoration power as it does for a civil suit, the power must be exercised within a reasonable time in light of the circumstances and the effect of delay on property rights. The Court applied Ibrahimpatnam Taluk Vyavasaya Coolie Sangham v. K. Suresh Reddy, which held that a power exercisable at any time must be used within a reasonable time and that, in fraud cases, the period is assessed from discovery of fraud with regard to relevant circumstances. It also relied on Jai Mangal Oraon v. Mira Nayak, a decision under the same Act. Even assuming fraud, the lapse of about forty years was unreasonable.

predicates.tribal_land_restoration_proceeding: A person claiming through tribal landholders sought restoration through an administrative land-restoration process.
predicates.restoration_power_has_no_specific_deadli: The authority acted under a power that did not prescribe a specific period within which it had to be exercised.
predicates.transfer_predated_restoration_action_by_: The transfer challenged in the restoration proceeding occurred several decades before the authority acted.
predicates.unlawful_or_fraudulent_transfer_was_the_: The restoration claim was based on an allegation that the land had been transferred unlawfully or by a fraudulent method.

issues.definition: When tribal land restoration is sought under a power without a specific deadline, a transfer challenged decades later as unlawful or fraudulent cannot be acted upon if the delay is unreasonable.

issues.legal_issue: A later-enacted restriction on transfers does not make a transfer that occurred before the restriction took effect unlawful under that restriction when the restriction is not retrospective.
material_facts: The tenancy surrender and settlement took place in 1938.
Section 46, which restricted transfers by raiyats belonging to Scheduled Tribes, was introduced by an amendment that came into force in 1948.
The Court noted that Section 46 had no retrospective effect and that the transfer had not been shown to contravene another provision in force when it occurred.
issues.conclusion: The 1938 transfer could not be treated as contravening Section 46, which was not in force when the transfer occurred.
issues.legal_principle: Section 46 of the Chota Nagpur Tenancy Act, 1908, was introduced by the 1947 amendment with effect from 5 January 1948 and was not retrospective. In Jai Mangal Oraon v. Mira Nayak, the Court likewise recognized that the restriction did not apply to a surrender made before it came into force. The Court found no established contravention of another provision applicable to the transfer in this case.

predicates.restoration_proceeding_based_on_a_transf: A restoration proceeding relied on a legal restriction on transfers as a basis for challenging the transfer.
predicates.transfer_predated_the_restriction: The transfer occurred before the transfer restriction took effect.
predicates.the_restriction_has_no_retroactive_effec: The transfer restriction was not made applicable to transfers that occurred before it took effect.

issues.definition: A transfer made before a non-retrospective restriction took effect is not governed by that later restriction in a restoration proceeding.
